This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is filed by the claimant being aggrieved of award dated 25.04.2017, passed by learned II Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Chhindwara (M.P.), in Claim Case No.1800023/2016, on the ground that learned Tribunal has awarded inadequate compensation for an accident which took place on 29.08.2015, at about 4:30 P.M., when claimant was travelling on his motorcycle.

It is evident from the record that claimant was treated at Nagpur from 29.08.2015 to 12.09.2015,
where he was operated upon and plating was done.
He was also treated subsequently.

3. It is mentioned in the grounds of appeal that claimant suffered permanent disability to the extent of 40% as certified vide Ex.P1/30, certified by Dr. Jitendra B. Taori M.S. DNB Orthopedic Surgeon,
Nagpur, and, therefore, taking 40% permanent disability, compensation should have been awarded in favour of the claimant.
4. Nobody is appearing even for the respondents.
5. On perusal of record, it is evident that claimant did not examine the doctor in support of the disability certificate.

No expert witness was examined to point out the extent of functional disability in the light of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar [(2011) 1 SCC 343].
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After going through the record, when impugned award is analyzed, then it is evident that amounts awarded under the head of nutritious diet and attendant is inadequate.
Claimant will be entitled to a sum of Rs.16,000/- (Rupees Sixteen Thousand) @ Rs.4,000/- (Rupees Four Thousand) per month for a period of four months under the head of nutritious diet.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.13,000/- (Rupees Thirteen Thousand) under the head of nutritious diet.
In the same manner, claimant will be entitled to a sum of Rs.13,000/- (Rupees Thirteen Thousand) under the head of attendant.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.13,000/- (Rupees Thirteen Thousand) under the head of attendant.
Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.18,000/- (Rupees Eighteen Thousand) under the head of loss of earning.
Accident of lower limb takes 12 to 16 weeks to heal.

7. Looking to the date of the accident i.e. 29.08.2015, notional income can be taken at Rs.6,239/-
per month and, therefore, for a period of four months, loss of earning will be Rs.24,956/- rounded of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand).
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.7,000/- under this head.
Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of physio therapy, future treatment etc., under which head a sum of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) is awarded.
Since claimant took treatment at Nagpur, therefore, under the head of transport, another sum of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand ) is awarded.

8. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.48,000/-, which will be admissible in favour of the claimant, which will earn interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of Claim Petition till the date of actual payment.

9. It is made clear that claimant is not entitled to addition of any amount under the head of permanent disability on two grounds, namely, that certificate is not issued by the District Medical Board and secondly, no doctor has been examined to prove the extent of functional disability.
10.
In above terms, appeal is disposed of.
11. Let record of Claims Tribunal be sent back.
